what: Folding the pair table by the signed Frobenius group <pi, -1>
machine: the same host as the reach-versus-memory run
why_it_is_sound: The factor base is closed under pi and under negation, so the set of pair sums S is closed under both: pi(P+Q) = pi(P)+pi(Q) and -(P+Q) = (-P)+(-Q) are again sums of base points. A table answering 'is rest in S' therefore needs one key per orbit, not one per pair.
why_the_enumeration_is_complete: Walking i over one representative of each signed orbit and j over the whole base reaches every orbit of ordered pairs: given (P,Q), let g carry P to the representative R of its own orbit; then (R, gQ) lies in the same orbit and is enumerated. That holds whatever the stabilisers are, so there are no false negatives - only the factor two of redundancy that the unordered i <= j symmetry would remove.
the_canonical_key: 1 + min_k x^(2^k). Negation never moves the abscissa, since -(x,y) = (x,x+y), so the sign half of the fold is free and only the Frobenius orbit of the abscissa is searched: n-1 squarings and a running minimum, no memory.

what_it_buys.stored_pairs: 61.0x fewer at n = 61 (n, not 2n: the unordered symmetry is left unfolded)

what_it_costs.probe: 9.8x, and the canonicalisation is nearly all of it: n-1 squarings is about 830 ns serial on this machine, against a 115 ns probe.
what_it_costs.recovery: the O(|F|) summand scan grows with the wider base - 0.96 ms at |F| = 16592 against 12.61 ms at |F| = 177632 - and a scan pays it once per witness it finds, not once per decomposition.

the_honest_number: 2.0x faster per decomposed target at equal memory. Not the 61x the probe count suggests: the probe got 9.8x dearer and the recovery scan grew with the base, and those two eat most of it.
what_is_binding_now: The canonicalisation. It is a chain of n-1 squarings, and a squaring here is a spread plus eight reduction-table lookups. In a normal basis the Frobenius is a one-bit rotation, so the same minimum would be n rotations - tens of nanoseconds rather than hundreds - which would put a folded probe below an unfolded one and leave the 61x nearly intact. That is measured as an opportunity, not claimed as a result.
not_claimed: That the fold is worth 61x end to end; it is not, and the run above says so. That the 4 GiB widths were run end to end; they are the sizing law evaluated at that budget, and the timed pair is the 0.64/1.15 GiB one.
